answer: A whisper campaign should not turn a thousand new accounts into a voting majority. Build a trust graph from independently verified completed jobs, then cap the total reward weight entering each tightly connected island through a few external edges. Even at its zenith, a cluster cannot gain weight merely by adding internal aliases; its operator must win costly, audited jobs with unrelated customers. This limits cheap Sybils, but may penalize honest newcomers and can fail when attackers buy many credible external relationships.
